unit.title: Place Value and Rounding
unit.blurb: Multiplying and dividing by 0.1 and 0.01, and rounding to decimal places and significant figures.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Multiply and divide integers and decimals by 0.1 and 0.01, and explain the effect.

O2.t: Round numbers to a given number of decimal places or significant figures.

p: Multiplying by **0.1** is the same as **dividing by 10**. Multiplying by **0.01** is the same as **dividing by 100**.
Dividing by **0.1** is the same as **multiplying by 10**. Dividing by **0.01** is the same as **multiplying by 100**.
0.1 is one tenth, so multiplying by 0.1 means finding one tenth of the number: 45 × 0.1 = 4.5 = 45 ÷ 10.
In the same way × 0.01 = ÷ 100, and ÷ 0.1 = × 10 (how many tenths are in 4.5? 45).
Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes a positive number **smaller**. Dividing by a number less than 1 makes it **bigger**. Use this to check.

p: To round to a number of **decimal places** (d.p.), look at the next digit: **5 or more** rounds up, **4 or less** keeps the digit.
3.4782 to 2 d.p. → look at the third decimal (8) → 3.48. Keep the zeros you need: 2.698 to 2 d.p. is **2.70**.
The **first significant figure** is the first digit that is not zero. 0.004 52 has first significant figure 4.
Round 48 361 to 2 s.f.: 48 000 (keep the place value with zeros). Round 0.006 829 to 2 s.f.: 0.0068.
Decimal places count from the decimal point; significant figures count from the first non-zero digit. 0.004 572 to 2 s.f. is 0.0046 – the zeros at the front only show the size.
Use significant figures to keep the same accuracy for very big or very small numbers.
Rounding 3876 to 1 s.f. gives 4000, not 4. The rounded number must be about the same size.
